newsitem.title: BULGARIA: FOCUS - Bulgaria wins $650 mln IMF funding accord.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Bulgaria wins $650 mln IMF funding accord.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) and Bulgaria's interim cabinet on Monday announced an accord on financial reform and funding worth more than $650 million to stabilise the shattered economy over the next year.

IMF mission leader Anne McGuirk told a news conference a strict fixed exchange rate system would be introduced in June to restore confidence in the lev currency. The package also includes $148 million to buy grain to ease shortages.
The IMF suspended disbursements of funding last year because of the former Socialist government's failure to meet reform targets.

That government was toppled by mass protests last month. Its prime minister Zhan Videnov has been barred from travelling abroad pending investigation of his role in sanctioning big grain exports in 1995 which led to the present crisis.

An IMF statement said a new standby arrangement of 372 million SDRs would be worth about $510 million, and 107 million SDRs would be made available under the cereals component of the IMF's emergency Compensatory and Contingency Financing Facility to finance grain imports.
The agreement is expected to pave the way for fresh financing from other donors, and talks on a rescheduling of Bulgaria's debt to the Paris Club of government creditors.
McGuirk said the programme would need to be supported by strong budgt and monetary policies, but would provide for wage and pension increases and assistance for those hardest hit by the crisis.

"There is also a strong commitment in the programme to structural reforms, in particular an ambitious privatisation programme both with regard to the banking system and the enterprise sector," she said.
McGuirk said she would travel to Brussels on Wednesday to prepare a consultative group meeting of lenders in the first week of April to win financing commitments for the programme.

She said the agreement should then go before the IMF board in the second week of April. The IMF said a first disbursement of $180 million would be released soon after the IMF board approved the agreement.

The new accord was drawn up with the interim cabinet that will hold office until after the April 19 general elections. The mission also met political parties to ensure the programme would be continued after the elections.
Monthly inflation hit 242.7 percent in February as the lev tumbled to historic lows of 3,000 to the dollar, but the lev has since recovered to around 1,600 to the dollar.
Finance Minister Svetoslav Gavriiski told the same news conference he expected inflation of less than 50 percent in March.

Among the first tasks of the new parliament will be passing a state budget and the necessary legal amendments to permit introduction of the currency board mechanism. This will match levs in circulation to central bank foreign currency reserves, severely restricting the government's financial policy and preventing it from printing money.
McGuirk said measures would be taken at the same time to overhaul Bulgaria's banking system. Insolvency cases are pending against 14 banks.

"We agreed on immediate steps to strengthen any weaknesses in the state banks and we have agreed financing resources of about $50 million dollars that would be available in the period immediately ahead," McGuirk said.
She said the lev would be fixed at around the market rate when the currency board was introduced, while interim prime minister Stefan Sofianski said it would be tied to the dollar.
Asked about the prospects for a reduction of Bulgaria's domestic debt, McGuirk said the programme target was for an overall deficit of around four percent of gross domestic product.
"The government should have sufficient resources to begin to reduce this debt burden simply by retiring the debt as it falls due and this should help to bring interest rates down," she said.
